title: Cinco maneras de aprender
source: Guiones y preguntas originales de Profesor Particular. Grabaciones sintéticas en inglés estadounidense.
options: Comments from other people changed the speaker's work.
Teaching someone else improved the speaker's own understanding.
A friend's recommendation made the speaker join the activity.
Broken equipment led the speaker to a useful new method.
Working more slowly improved the speaker's final result.
A strict deadline helped the speaker finish the project.
Short, regular practice was more effective than long sessions.
The speaker decided to study alone instead of attending lessons.

speakers.transcript: At the start of my pottery course, I saved all my practice for Sunday afternoons. That gave me plenty of time, but by the next week I had forgotten how to shape the clay. My teacher suggested spending just fifteen minutes at the wheel each evening. I was sceptical because it felt too little to matter. After a month, the movements had become much easier, and I no longer needed to look at my notes. Short, regular sessions worked far better for me than one long weekly session.
speakers.why: Compara las largas sesiones de los domingos con quince minutos diarios y afirma que la práctica breve y regular funcionó mejor.

speakers.transcript: I planned to photograph a local market using my tripod, but one of its legs broke on the first morning. At first I thought I would have to cancel the project. Then I tried holding the camera and moving through the market instead. I could follow people more naturally and wait for moments I would never have noticed from a fixed position. My pictures were less formal, but they told a better story. Now I often choose that approach even when the tripod is working.
speakers.why: La rotura del trípode le obligó a probar la fotografía cámara en mano; descubrió que contaba mejor la historia.

speakers.transcript: I had grown herbs on my balcony for years, so I agreed to show my younger neighbour how to start. She kept asking why I watered one plant more than another. I realised I could do it by instinct but could not explain it properly. I read about the different plants, made simple notes and tried answering her questions again. My own plants improved as a result. Helping her understand the basics taught me more than another season of gardening by myself would have done.
speakers.why: Al enseñar a su vecina tuvo que investigar y explicar sus decisiones, y eso mejoró su propio aprendizaje.

speakers.transcript: I shared a short song at an online music workshop. I expected everyone to comment on the sound quality, because I had used a cheap microphone. Instead, several listeners said that the melody was difficult to follow in the middle. They pointed to the same section, so I knew I should listen carefully. I rewrote the chorus and played it again the following week. The response was much warmer. Letting other people hear the first version helped me notice a problem I had missed.
speakers.why: Los comentarios del público señalaron un problema de melodía y le llevaron a reescribir el estribillo.

speakers.transcript: For my first woodwork project, I wanted to make a small box as quickly as possible. I cut the pieces before checking the measurements twice, and the sides did not fit together. My instructor did not give me a new design. She asked me to mark each cut carefully and stop whenever I felt rushed. The next box took much longer, but its corners finally matched. I had thought speed was a sign of progress. Now I know that accuracy matters more to me.
speakers.why: Al dejar de apresurarse y comprobar las medidas, consiguió que las piezas encajaran mejor.
